item.name: Auth
item.description:
JWT authentication endpoints.

User accounts are not created through the API. To create a user:
• Django admin UI: http://localhost:8000/admin/
• Management command: python manage.py createsuperuser

Once a user exists, obtain a token pair with POST /auth/token/ and include the access token as a Bearer token on all subsequent requests. Access tokens expire — use POST /auth/token/refresh/ with the refresh token to get a new one without re-entering credentials.

response.name: 401 Unauthorized — Invalid credentials
401 Unauthorized — Invalid or expired refresh token

request.description: Flip the per-environment kill switch (EnvironmentFlag.is_enabled) for the named environment. The state is created on first toggle (off by default), invalidates the flag cache, and writes an audit entry.
Pin one user to a variation, overriding rules and rollout. 201 on create, 200 when re-targeting. Point at the true/fallthrough variation for an allowlist, the false/off variation for a denylist.
Gate this flag behind another serving a specific variation. Returns 409 if it would close a cycle.
Append-only: writes a new rollback version rather than rewriting history.

operator choices: eq, neq, contains, in, not_in, gt, lt

serve_variation: null for boolean flags (returns true on match). For multivariate flags, set to a variation ID to serve a specific variation when this rule matches.

request.description:
Every flag in the SDK key's environment, resolved for one user context in a single call — what an SDK asks for at session start instead of one request per flag.

Auth: X-SDK-Key header. Set {{sdk_key}} via Create SDK Key or Rotate SDK Key — the test script auto-saves it.

Flags are keyed by flag key so a client looks one up by name. variation_id is null for a flag with no variations configured.

Same engine as POST /sdk/evaluate/: kill switch, prerequisites, individual targets, rules, and rollout all apply identically.

Archived flags, and flags not configured in this environment, are omitted rather than reported as errors — an environment with no flags returns 200 with an empty object, not a 404.

POST rather than GET because the user context is an arbitrary nested object: query-string encoding is lossy and would put user attributes into access logs and proxy caches.

Throttled on its own scope (evaluation_bulk, default 120/min) because one call does the work of N single evaluations.

Logs no impressions. A bootstrap is a download, not a read — the app may go on to use three of fifty flags. Impressions arrive through the batching endpoint instead.

Costs one round trip per user context, which suits one user per session (a browser SDK). A server-side SDK evaluating thousands of users in-process wants GET /sdk/flags/config/ instead — see SDK_CONFIG_SPEC.md.
